reference: GNU Bash builtin metadata/help conventions; util-linux findmnt reading the same synthetic mountinfo fixture with --tab-file --raw --noheadings and the ID,PARENT,MAJ:MIN,FSROOT,TARGET,VFS-OPTIONS,FSTYPE,SOURCE columns; util-linux mountpoint for mountpoint state/device-number checks. The findmnt adapter maps its raw space-separated fields to the builtin's tab-separated table and decodes findmnt's raw \x20 spelling to the literal spaces produced by decoding mountinfo's \040 escape.
coverage: Bash recognizes bashmount as an enabled builtin and exposes its long help text.
Synthetic mountinfo parsing with and without optional fields before the separator, including VFS options and source fields.
Kernel octal escape decoding for spaces in mount target and source, independently compared with findmnt raw output.
Empty mountinfo table and missing table path behavior.
Mountpoint device number for the private fixture working directory and quiet classification of a regular file.
Empty table returns status 1 without rows, matching findmnt no-match behavior.
exclusions: No mount(2), umount2(2), bind, recursive bind, remount, or propagation operation is executed; these have explicit deferred VM/mock cases.
The live /proc/self/mountinfo listing path (-l) is not compared; table parsing is exercised against deterministic relative fixture files instead.

Block-device mountpoint mode (-x), fstab, UUID/LABEL source resolution, real devices, and kernel-specific filesystem behavior are not exercised. UUID/LABEL and fstab handling are documented as outside the v1 implementation.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify the statically enabled command as a builtin.
Bash help must use bashmount's configured static short description and expose the full documented options text.
cases.stdout:
bashmount: bashmount [-t TYPE] [-o OPTS] [-B|-R|--remount|-u|-l|--mountpoint|--findmnt-table] SRC DST
    Mount/umount filesystems and list /proc/self/mountinfo.
    
        bashmount [-t TYPE] [-o OPTS] SRC DST
        bashmount -B SRC DST              # bind mount
        bashmount -R SRC DST              # recursive bind mount
        bashmount --remount [-o OPTS] DST
        bashmount -l                       # list mounts
        bashmount -u [-l|-f] DST           # umount (-l detach, -f force)
        bashmount --mountpoint [-q|-d|-x] PATH
        bashmount --findmnt-table [PATH]
        bashmount -h | --help
    
    OPTS is a comma-separated subset of:
        ro / rw / nosuid / nodev / noexec / noatime / nodiratime /
        relatime / strictatime / sync / dirsync / mand / bind / remount /
        shared / private / slave / unbindable / rec
    Unknown tokens are passed as fs-specific data (e.g. tmpfs size=64m).

cases.purpose: Parse ordinary mountinfo rows, both with no optional fields and with multiple optional fields before the dash; retain the specified eight tab-separated columns.
Decode Linux mountinfo's \040 representation in target and source fields while preserving the tab-delimited output structure.
Compare the zero-byte table boundary with GNU findmnt's empty-file status; both sides must emit no rows and the expected status is checked against findmnt.
Compare the actual reference exit status, output and diagnostic policy for a missing table.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then
 bashmount --findmnt-table absent
else
 findmnt --tab-file absent --raw --noheadings -o ID,PARENT,MAJ:MIN,FSROOT,TARGET,VFS-OPTIONS,FSTYPE,SOURCE
fi

cases.purpose: For the fixture tree's current mountpoint, print the same major:minor device number as util-linux mountpoint using only the relative path '.'.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then
  bashmount --mountpoint -d .
else
  mountpoint -d .
fi

cases.purpose: Compare quiet non-mountpoint classification and its actual util-linux exit status on a private regular file.
cases.script:
: > regular
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then
 bashmount --mountpoint --quiet regular
else
 mountpoint --quiet regular
fi

cases.purpose: Exercise plain typed mounts, option flag mapping, and filesystem-specific data forwarding.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated mount namespace and disposable tmpfs target, or a reviewed mount(2) mock that records source, target, type, flags, and data. The fixture must verify successful tmpfs mount effects and option combinations such as ro,nosuid,size=64k without touching host mounts.

cases.purpose: Exercise bind, recursive bind, and remount behavior including read-only follow-up remount handling.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with nested fixture mountpoints in a private mount namespace, or a reviewed syscall mock that records both mount(2) calls and their flags. Verify -B, -R, --remount, and bind plus ro semantics without changing host mounts.

cases.purpose: Exercise ordinary, lazy, and force unmount flag mapping and observable cleanup.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with disposable private-namespace mounts, or a reviewed umount2(2) mock that records flags. Verify normal, -l/MNT_DETACH, and -f/MNT_FORCE calls and cleanup/error behavior; no unmount operation is run in this suite.

cases.purpose: Quietly classify a private subdirectory without mounting anything.
cases.script:
mkdir sub
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then bashmount --mountpoint -q sub; else mountpoint -q sub; fi

cases.purpose: A device-number query on an ordinary private subdirectory returns the util-linux non-mountpoint status and stdout message; no mount operation occurs.
cases.script:
mkdir sub
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then bashmount --mountpoint -d sub; else mountpoint -d sub; fi

cases.purpose: Default classification messages retain the caller-supplied relative names for a private directory and the fixture mount; only queries run.
cases.script:
mkdir sub
if [[ $(type -t bashmount) == builtin ]]; then
 if bashmount --mountpoint sub; then exit 90; else [[ $? == 32 ]]; fi
 bashmount --mountpoint .
else
 if mountpoint sub; then exit 90; else [[ $? == 32 ]]; fi
 mountpoint .
fi
